title: Runes overview
text: Runes is a fungible token protocol carved into Bitcoin transactions. A runestone in an OP_RETURN output etches, mints, or transfers. Balances live in UTXOs. Activated at block 840000 at the fourth halving in April 2024.

title: The protocol in one look
text: Rune balances ride on transaction outputs. The runestone is an instruction, not a vault. Inputs carry balances, edicts allocate them to outputs.

title: What a runestone can do
text: Etch creates a rune and fixes name, divisibility, symbol, premine, and terms. Mint creates units while terms hold. Transfer moves balances with edicts and a pointer.

title: How runes are identified
text: A rune ID is BLOCK:TX, the etching block and the transaction index within it. The first rune UNCOMMON GOODS is hardcoded with ID 1:0 and symbol U+29C9.

title: Source and ecosystem
text: Owning repository bitcoinuniverseio slash runes. Reference implementation ord by the Ordinals project. Central docs platform docs.bitcoinuniverse.io.

title: Runes specification
text: Numbered normative rules for encoding, parsing, and validating runestones, grounded in ord 0.29.0 and the ordinals crate 0.0.17.

title: 1 Carrier and transaction anatomy
text: A runestone output script begins OP_RETURN 0x6a followed by OP_13 0x5d. The first matching output is the runestone. At most one per transaction. Payload is the concatenation of all data pushes.

title: 2 Varint encoding
text: The payload decodes to unsigned 128-bit integers as LEB128 varints, at most 19 bytes each. Overlong, Overflow, and Unterminated failures all make the transaction a cenotaph with flaw Varint.

title: 3 Message structure
text: Integers parse as tag and value pairs until the Body tag 0. Repeated tags accumulate into a queue. Everything after Body is edict groups of exactly four integers.

title: 4 Tag table
text: Body 0, Flags 2, Rune 4, Premine 6, Cap 8, Amount 10, HeightStart 12, HeightEnd 14, OffsetStart 16, OffsetEnd 18, Mint 20, Pointer 22, Cenotaph 126, Divisibility 1, Spacers 3, Symbol 5, Nop 127. Even tags must be understood; odd tags may be ignored.

title: 5 Flags
text: Tag 2 is a bitfield. Bit 0 Etching, bit 1 Terms, bit 2 Turbo, bit 127 reserved. Any bit still set after consumption gives flaw UnrecognizedFlag.

title: 6 Etching
text: Names are A to Z in modified base 26, one to twenty-six letters. Values at or above 6402364363415443603228541259936211926 are reserved. Divisibility at most 38. Etching requires a taproot tapscript commitment with at least 6 confirmations.

title: 7 Minting
text: The Mint tag is given twice, block then transaction index. A mint succeeds when the rune exists and its height window and cap allow. A failed mint is ignored, not a cenotaph.

title: 8 Edicts and delta encoding
text: Each edict is four integers: block delta, transaction index or delta, amount, output. IDs accumulate from 0:0. Amount 0 means the whole remaining balance. Output equal to the output count is a split.

title: 9 Pointer
text: The pointer must be less than the output count. Remaining unallocated runes go to the pointer output, otherwise the first non-OP_RETURN output, otherwise they are burned.

title: 10 State transitions
text: The unallocated pool is input balances plus mint plus premine. Allocations to an OP_RETURN output are burned. Balances are per rune per outpoint in atomic units.

title: 11 Cenotaphs
text: A cenotaph burns all input runes, makes an etched rune unmintable, and burns mint output while still counting the mint against the cap. Ten flaws: Opcode, InvalidScript, Varint, TruncatedField, TrailingIntegers, UnrecognizedEvenTag, UnrecognizedFlag, SupplyOverflow, EdictRuneId, EdictOutput.

title: 12 Hardcoded genesis rune
text: UNCOMMON GOODS, rune ID 1:0, name value 2055900680524219742, spacers 128, symbol U+29C9, amount 1 per mint, cap u128 max, height window 840000 to 1050000.

title: Runes guide
text: Plain-language walkthrough with worked byte-level examples for every runestone operation.

title: The mental model
text: A rune balance is a property of a transaction output, like a satoshi amount. Spend the output and you spend the runes. The runestone says where they land.

title: Transfer, worked
text: A single edict transfer decoded byte by byte: OP_RETURN, OP_13, push length, Body tag, block delta, transaction index, amount, output. Change follows the default rule to output 0.

title: Splitting and sweeping
text: Amount 0 means the entire remaining balance. An output index equal to the output count splits across all non-OP_RETURN outputs. One higher is a cenotaph.

title: Mint, worked
text: Minting needs only the Mint tag given twice. A closed mint produces a confirmed transaction that creates nothing and refunds nothing.

title: Etch, worked
text: A full etching with flags, name, divisibility, spacers, symbol, premine, amount, cap, and offset end, decoded field by field. Etching needs a commit transaction and a six block wait.

title: Ways an etching quietly fails
text: A name already etched, a name still locked at this height, or a missing or immature commitment all make the etching disappear without a cenotaph.

title: Burning
text: Runes are burned by sending them to an OP_RETURN output with an edict or pointer. The accidental way is a cenotaph, which burns everything in the inputs.

title: What to check before you sign
text: Decode the runestone, confirm output 0 is yours, keep rune outputs above dust, know which inputs you are spending, and confirm the mint is open.

title: Support in Bitcoin Universe products
text: Runes are read-only first-party data in Bitcoin Universe products. Viewing, discovery, and activity are supported. Listing, buying, settlement, etching, minting, and transferring from inside Universe apps are not currently supported.

title: Runes reference
text: Terminology, indexer semantics, confirmation and reorg behavior, sizes, limitations, security considerations, and an implementation checklist.

title: Terminology
text: Runestone, artifact, cenotaph, flaw, etching, rune ID, edict, pointer, premine, terms, turbo, atomic unit, unallocated pool, reserved name, commitment.

title: Indexer pipeline
text: Per transaction: drain input balances, apply the mint, apply the etching and premine, process edicts, assign the remainder, record burns. Cenotaph status discards all allocation.

title: Terms evaluation
text: Start is the larger of HeightStart and etching block plus OffsetStart. End is the smaller of HeightEnd and etching block plus OffsetEnd, exclusive. An absent cap is zero, so terms without a cap are unmintable.

title: Confirmation and mempool
text: Confirmed blocks are the only truth. Transaction order within a block matters. There is no mempool consensus, so unconfirmed rune activity is provisional. Etching needs 6 confirmations on its commitment.

title: Reorg behavior
text: Rune state is derived from the chain and handled by rewinding to a savepoint and re-indexing. Rune IDs, mint counts, and balances can all move backwards. Key caches by block hash, not height.

title: Sizes and fees
text: Runestone script sizes from 2 bytes empty to 89 bytes for a maximal etching. The reference wallet refuses scripts over 83 bytes by default, a relay policy rather than a protocol rule. Output count dominates cost.

title: Limitations
text: Names are permanently unique and first-come. Etched properties are immutable with no admin key. One runestone per transaction. No conditional logic, royalties, freeze, or clawback.

title: Security considerations
text: Cenotaphs burn silently and totally. The default destination sends unallocated runes to output 0. Rune-unaware coin selection destroys value. Identify runes by ID, not name. Etching is racy.

title: Implementation checklist
text: Thirteen steps from searching outputs for OP_RETURN OP_13 through varint decoding, tag consumption order, etching preconditions, the allocation pipeline, burns, persistence, reorg handling, and verifying against the test vectors.

title: Test vectors
text: Twenty-four verified cases as complete output script hex: eight valid runestones, fourteen cenotaphs covering all ten flaws, and two non-runestone scripts.

title: Valid runestones
text: Empty runestone, single edict transfer, two delta encoded edicts, sweep with amount zero, even split, mint, mint with pointer, and a full etching.

title: Cenotaph vectors
text: Fourteen cenotaph cases covering Opcode, InvalidScript, Varint, TruncatedField, TrailingIntegers, UnrecognizedEvenTag, UnrecognizedFlag, SupplyOverflow, EdictRuneId, and EdictOutput.

title: Not runestones
text: Scripts that produce no artifact at all. A transaction with no artifact transfers balances normally, while a cenotaph burns them.

title: Values that are ignored, not fatal
text: Divisibility above 38, spacers above 0x07FFFFFF, and a symbol that is not a Unicode scalar are all ignored silently on odd tags. The same failure on an even tag is a cenotaph.

title: Beyond the payload
text: Cases needing transaction or chain fixtures: missing or immature commitments, taken or locked names, unnamed etchings, closed mints, runestones in later outputs, and edicts with rune ID 0:0.

title: Runestone decoder
text: Paste a runestone OP_RETURN script hex and read the decoded tags, etching, mint, edicts, and pointer, with cenotaph flaws explained. Runs entirely in your browser.

title: Decoder examples
text: Buttons that load test vectors directly into the decoder, covering valid runestones and cenotaphs.

title: What the decoder checks
text: Carrier, pushes, varints, message structure, field consumption order, and supply overflow. It cannot check chain state such as name availability or whether a mint is open.

title: Decoder privacy
text: No third-party requests, no analytics, no fonts, no network calls. Pasted script hex never leaves the page.

text: Version history of this documentation and the protocol milestones it describes.

title: Protocol milestones
text: Proposed in 2023 by Casey Rodarmor. Activated at block 840000 in April 2024. Name minimums step down every 17500 blocks until all names unlock at block 1050000.

title: How this documentation is versioned
text: Major for structural or rule numbering changes, minor for added sections, patch for corrections. Every footer carries the document version and the ord version it is grounded in.
